description: We are SOL404, a team passionate about technology, space exploration, and creative innovation. Our mission is to bring NASA's forgotten lunar and Martian equipment back to life through an immersive web experience combining cinematic storytelling, interactive exploration, and real scientific discoveries. We're looking for creative minds skilled in web development, UI/UX, 3D design, scientific research, and storytelling. Join us to turn forgotten missions into unforgettable experiences!
summary:
After the Signal is an interactive educational terminal experience developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, addressing the storytelling challenge regarding NASA's discarded and silent equipment on the Moon and Mars.
The web application invites visitors to enter a fictional recovery terminal featuring a simulated 15-second power reserve and an IGNITE command. Once power fails, it unlocks a chronological archive of 17 curated missions, combining first-person narrative writing, official NASA imagery, and readable scientific records with dual reading levels (Kids and Deep Dive)
This project is vital because it shifts the narrative around inactive hardware, teaching students and space enthusiasts that an abandoned machine is not a failed mission, but an enduring scientific and technological legacy
details:
Project Overview & Functionality After the Signal is an English-language educational terminal experience about NASA equipment that stopped answering, stayed behind, or completed its work. Built around 17 curated mission and hardware records, visitors enter a fictional recovery terminal featuring a simulated 15-second power reserve and an IGNITE command. When power fails, it unlocks a chronological archive containing short first-person narratives, terminal-style typing, official NASA imagery, and readable scientific records
Benefits & Intended Impact The project raises public awareness about the legacy of NASA's silent explorers, teaching users that an inactive machine is not necessarily a failed mission. It clearly separates imagined narrative writing from real mission facts, offering dual reading levels (Kids and Deep Dive) and robust accessibility options like Safe Mode (which removes visual CRT/glitch effects and supports reduced-motion preferences).
Tools & Technologies Used
Frontend & Runtime: React 19, Vite 8, TypeScript 6, and CSS Modules.
APIs & Data: Native browser fetch and Web Audio APIs, alongside self-contained Vercel serverless function routes connecting to NASA Image and Video Library, NSSDCA Master Catalog, and NASA/JPL Horizons.
Assets & Credits: Features official Moon and Mars global mosaics, with a credited third-party artist-rendered lunar diorama video (The Moon Landing V.2 by MisterH, licensed under CC BY 4.0).
Creativity & Design Factors The team prioritized historical accuracy, scientific boundaries, and seamless mobile responsiveness (utilizing dynamic viewport heights and iOS zoom prevention). The experience avoids compulsory quizzes or collection checklists, focusing instead on immersive storytelling, transparent source attribution, local device persistence, and easy mission report sharing via clipboard.
